title: Echo of a callable compiles and throws a RuntimeError that names an internal class.
text: `callable $f = fn(): int => 1; echo $f;` passes `nvs check`, and the run throws `RuntimeError` "cannot convert an object of class `Script$fn0` to `string`: it does not implement `Stringable`". A `callable` never has a string form, so the checker can know this, as it does for `void` with `E0707`, and `Script$fn0` is a name the program never wrote. It closes when a `callable` after `echo` or `.` is `E0707`, with a conformance case.
